I hope you stick around. If you find crosswords aren't your thing, that's just the way it goes. But give yourself some time to learn the ropes. And, as you might have noticed, Monday puzzles are the easiest, with more straightforward cluing and a theme that ties everything together. They get harder (and trickier) throughout the week. But crossword puzzlers are a pretty encouraging group, so I hope to hear from you again.

I also know it as jerryrig, and was stumped when it didn’t fit. I had to get it from the crosses and then go online to confirm that JURYRIG is an actual accepted spelling. 

When I think of jury rigging, I imagine someone slipping an envelope of cash to the foreperson. (Unless the foreperson’s name is Jerry. Then I guess that could be Jerry rigging, too.)

As a craftsman I have always understood jury rig to mean that you're making the most of the materials available to you in a particular situation. As opposed to jerry rig which I have always understood to mean fabricating something from inferior materials in a shoddy manor. So it made sense to me that the fill would be jury rig in relation to the clue.

That is how I've seen it (or even used it.)  If you watch 5 minutes of America's Funniest Home Videos, you will see at least one JERRY-rigged "solution" (and the consequences, which I really don't think are funny!  Ouch!)

Actually, it appears that jerry rig and jury rig are slightly different, perhaps with an emphasis on "slightly." https://www.merriam-webster.com/grammar/jerry-built-vs-jury-rigged-vs-jerry-rigged-usage-history
